adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — original` comes from getById (line 91), which is wrapped so that isEnabled() is false while its org, or the realm's organizations feature, is disabled; an update made during that time that removes login eligibility (BROKER_PUBLIC=false, hideOnLogin, linkOnly) finds both predicates false and skips invalidation, but the JPA-backed cached list still holds the IDP id; once the org is re-enabled, the private/hidden broker appears on the login page because the bean only re-checks isEnabled()

adjudication.rationale: The new login-IDP list cache in `getForLogin` returns providers purely by cached internal IDs and does not re-apply `getLoginPredicate()` when serving from cache (it just does `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` and returns the set). Cache invalidation on update is guarded by `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`, which explicitly skips invalidation when both `getLoginPredicate().test(original)` and `.test(updated)` are false. Since `update()` obtains `original` via `getById(model.getInternalId())` (which, per surrounding changes, can be “wrapped”/organization-aware), a wrapper-induced `isEnabled()`/login-state change can make both predicates false even when the underlying login-eligibility changed, causing the cached ID list to remain stale. The bean change only re-checks `idp.isEnabled()` (not other login-eligibility flags), so a stale cached ID can surface on the login page when the wrapper conditions change later. This is a correctness bug in the cache invalidation + cache serving path introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:239 — Race: the new query copies every searchKey from the previously read `query`; if a writer's invalidation lands between cache.get and invalidateObject, the bumped revision matches `loaded`, so pre-write results for other orgs are put back into the cache and stay stale

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin`, when `query != null` but `query.getIDPs(searchKey) == null`, the code does `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then builds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., query)` which (by API shape) merges/copies prior cached search results from the previously read `query`. If an external writer invalidation for `cacheKey` happens after the initial `cache.get(cacheKey, ...)` but before this thread reconstructs and `addRevisioned(...)`, then `loaded = cache.getCurrentRevision(cacheKey)` will observe the bumped revision while the merged data still contains pre-invalidation results for other `searchKey`s. That can repopulate stale entries under the new revision, defeating the invalidation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — All orgs share one per-realm key for ALL/ORG_ONLY, so the first lookup for each org evicts the entry and copies the whole map; under concurrent logins across many orgs, requests keep evicting each other's entries (addRevisioned is skipped), the cache thrashes, and the entry grows without limit (one set per org, each repeating all realm-level ids)

adjudication.rationale: In `getForLogin(...)`, the cache key is per-realm and per-`FetchMode` only (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), not per organization. The code then stores per-organization results inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` keyed by `searchKey` (`organizationId` or ""). When an org-specific entry is missing (`cached == null`), it invalidates the whole cached object (`cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`) and recreates it with the previous query chained (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`), meaning different org lookups contend over the same cache entry and each new org causes full invalidation/rewrite. Also, because each distinct `organizationId` becomes a new `searchKey`, the cached structure can grow with the number of orgs queried. This is a diff-grounded scalability/performance design concern; it’s not a directly verifiable functional correctness break from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:370 — The test asserts only cache internals (IdentityProviderListQuery set sizes) and never the IDPs getForLogin actually returns; it does not cover removing or creating a login IDP or updates while the org is disabled, so wrong or stale cached results would still pass

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the assertions after calling `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` only inspect cache state (`IdentityProviderListQuery` existence and `getIDPs(...).size()`), and never materialize/assert the actual returned `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` contents. This means the test primarily validates that the cache is populated/invalidated with expected counts, not that `getForLogin` returns the correct IDPs when served from cache. Also, the test exercises removal of a non-login IDP (`idp-alias-1` is disabled) but does not cover removal of an IDP that qualifies for login. The mention of "updates while the org is disabled" is not evidenced in the diff.

model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:93 — update() tests getLoginPredicate against the org-aware wrapped getById model, whose isEnabled() is false when the org is disabled, so disabling/hiding/link-only/unpublishing such an IDP skips login-cache invalidation and getForLogin keeps returning it (the bean only re-checks isEnabled) once the org is re-enabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds selective login-cache invalidation in update() via registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(idpById, model), where the decision is based on getLoginPredicate().test(original/updated) (and orgId equality). The diff also notes elsewhere that an IDP "might have been wrapped" and needs isEnabled() re-checking, implying wrappers can alter enabled-ness. If getById() returns an organization-aware wrapper whose isEnabled() can vary (e.g., when an org is disabled), then using getLoginPredicate() on that potentially context-sensitive `original` can cause the early-return paths to skip invalidation even though underlying IDP login-availability-related config changed, leaving stale IDs in the getForLogin cache. However, the diff does not show getById()’s wrapping behavior or org-disable semantics, so the claimed broken behavior can’t be fully verified from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The public SPI getLoginPredicate() now also drops non-public org brokers, but the LoginFilter/getForLogin javadoc and getLoginSearchOptions() were not updated, so the predicate and search options now disagree and external callers (e.g. federatedProviderPredicate overrides) pick up the stricter filter without notice.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes the public SPI `LoginFilter.getLoginPredicate()` to additionally filter out org-linked IDPs unless `BROKER_PUBLIC` is true (`.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`). That is a behavior/contract change for any external caller that reuses this predicate. The diff does not show any corresponding update to `getLoginSearchOptions()` or any javadoc, so the concern about SPI semantics changing without the related API/docs/options being adjusted is a concrete review issue (though the javadoc/options mismatch itself isn’t directly verifiable from the shown context).

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The cached getForLogin path returns a HashSet stream in arbitrary order, while the invalidated path returns the delegate's ordered stream, so SPI callers see different element order depending on cache state.

adjudication.rationale: In the new cached `getForLogin` implementation, IDs are collected into a `Set` (`Collectors.toSet()`), then resolved into a `HashSet<IdentityProviderModel>` and returned via `identityProviders.stream()` (see added method around `getForLogin`). This loses any encounter/order the delegate stream might have had, so the element order can differ between the cached path and the invalidated path (`return idpDelegate.getForLogin(...).map(...)`). However, the diff does not show an SPI/contract requirement that `getForLogin` preserves a stable ordering, so it’s an inconsistency/behavioral concern rather than a provable correctness defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — update() evaluates getLoginPredicate on the org-aware wrapper from getById (isEnabled folds in org/feature enabled state) while the cached list comes from DB flags only, so changing hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC on an IDP linked to a disabled org skips invalidation and the stale entry shows up again once the org is re-enabled (the bean only re-checks isEnabled)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds login-IDP caching plus selective invalidation in update() via registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(original, updated). In update(), `original` is obtained via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, i.e. through the caching/session layer, while `updated` is the raw model passed in. The invalidation decision is based on `getLoginPredicate().test(...)`, and the UI bean explicitly notes that returned IDPs "might have been wrapped" and therefore re-checks only `isEnabled()`. If `getById()` returns an organization-aware wrapper whose `isEnabled()` depends on org state, `getLoginPredicate()` can evaluate differently for `original` than for the underlying stored IDP flags used to build the cached list (the cache stores internal IDs from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`). That can cause the method to hit the `(!pred(original) && !pred(updated)) return;` fast-path and skip invalidating login caches when DB-level login-relevant flags (e.g., hideOnLogin/linkOnly/BROKER_PUBLIC) change while the org is disabled, leaving a stale cached internalId set that later becomes visible again when the org is re-enabled (since the bean only re-checks `isEnabled`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:409 — Changing BROKER_PUBLIC on a realm-level IDP never invalidates the login caches (the new predicate treats orgId==null as qualifying either way), but the default getForLogin(ORG_ONLY/ALL, null) query adds no orgId-not-null filter, so its results change and cached and uncached results drift apart

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes BROKER_PUBLIC irrelevant for realm-level IDPs: `getLoginPredicate()` now explicitly allows any IDP with `getOrganizationId() == null` regardless of `BROKER_PUBLIC` (`idp.getOrganizationId() == null || ...BROKER_PUBLIC...`). Therefore toggling BROKER_PUBLIC on an IDP with `organizationId == null` does not change whether it qualifies for login, so there is no demonstrated need to invalidate the new `cacheKeyForLogin(...)` entries in that scenario. The claim that ORG_ONLY/ALL queries with `organizationId == null` change results due to BROKER_PUBLIC (and thus cached vs uncached drift) is not verifiable from this diff, and contradicts the predicate change shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — The merge path re-adds the previously read query's per-org sets under a newly bumped revision, so an invalidation committed concurrently between the read and invalidateObject can be undone and stale login IDP sets brought back

adjudication.rationale: In getForLogin(), when a cache entry exists but doesn’t contain the current `searchKey`, the code calls `cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)` and then immediately rebuilds and re-adds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery` that incorporates the previously read `query` (`new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., cached, query)`), effectively carrying forward all previously cached per-searchKey sets under a new revision. That behavior is visible in the diff and could undermine the intent of invalidation (and may have race/consistency implications), but whether it truly “undoes” a concurrent invalidation depends on `RealmCacheManager`/revision semantics not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The BROKER_PUBLIC clause is hardcoded in getLoginPredicate rather than modeled as a LoginFilter entry, so the predicate no longer matches getLoginSearchOptions or the enum javadoc ("all fields considered"), and the org-public rule now lives in three places (here, default getForLogin line 180, OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean line 68)

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:236 — The login cache uses one key per realm and mode, with a separate searchKey for each organizationId, so every newly seen org invalidates the shared entry, re-queries the DB, and copies all earlier org sets into the new entry; with many orgs the entry grows without bound (O(orgs^2) copying), and concurrent logins for different orgs keep evicting each other's rebuilds, unlike getByOrganization, which keys per org.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `getForLogin(FetchMode mode, String organizationId)`, the cache key is `cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)` (no org), while per-org results are stored under a `searchKey` inside a single `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry (`query.getIDPs(searchKey)`). When an orgId is first seen (`cached == null`), the code invalidates the shared entry (`cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey)`) and rebuilds a new `IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query)`, implying it carries forward prior cached org result sets into the new object. This design can cause the single entry to accumulate results for many orgIds and forces invalidation/rebuild on each newly seen org, which can lead to unbounded growth and cross-org contention/thrashing (unlike `getByOrganization`, which uses `cacheKeyOrgId(realm, orgId)` per org). The diff does not show an outright correctness failure, but it does introduce a concrete scalability/architecture concern grounded in the code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:386 — Creating, updating, or removing any login IDP in any org invalidates the cached login lists for every org and every FetchMode in the realm, so the whole list is rebuilt after each such change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds realm-scoped login list caching keyed only by realm+FetchMode (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), while per-organization results are stored inside the single `IdentityProviderListQuery` entry via `searchKey` (orgId or ""). Invalidation on create/remove (`registerIDPLoginInvalidation`) and on certain updates (`registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate`) loops over **all** `FetchMode.values()` and registers invalidation for `cacheKeyForLogin(...)` without any org scoping. Therefore, any qualifying login-IDP change clears the cached login lists for that realm for every org/searchKey and every FetchMode, forcing rebuild. This is a performance/scope concern, not a verifiable correctness defect in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:246 — On a cold or rebuilt entry, the full models the delegate already loaded are thrown away after taking their IDs and are then fetched again one at a time through getById, which costs N+1 DB queries per rebuild.
matched_golden_ids: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin() recursively calls session.identityProviders().getById() instead of idpDelegate.getById(), causing the cache lookup to re-enter the same caching layer.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that during cache rebuild the code discards already-loaded delegate models and then refetches each one via getById, causing redundant lookups (N+1) through the provider layer. This aligns with the golden issue’s core problem: calling session.identityProviders().getById() (re-entering the caching layer) instead of using the delegate directly, leading to unnecessary re-fetching.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:100 — remove() now always runs an extra DB getByAlias query, even when the IDP is already in the cache.

adjudication.rationale: In remove(String alias), the diff introduces an unconditional `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` before the cache validity check. Previously, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` was only invoked in the `isInvalid(cacheKey)` branch; the non-invalid branch relied on the cached entry. This change therefore adds an extra delegate lookup even when the IDP is present in cache (a likely performance regression). The diff doesn’t prove it always hits the DB, but it does prove the extra delegate call was added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:80 — The added idp.isEnabled() re-check on wrapped models triggers an OrganizationProvider.getById lookup for each org-linked IDP on every login page render.

adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:405 — Login-cache invalidation on update evaluates getLoginPredicate against the org-aware wrapped `idpById` (isEnabled()==false while its org is disabled). Once the org is re-enabled, the stale cached ID list shows the hidden, link-only, or private org broker on the login page, because the bean only re-checks isEnabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add selective login-cache invalidation on update (registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) based on getLoginPredicate(original/updated). However, the finding’s core premise—that `idpById` is an “org-aware wrapped” model whose `isEnabled()` becomes false when the organization is disabled, causing both predicates to be false and invalidation to be skipped—cannot be verified from this diff. The wrapper behavior and whether `getById()` returns such a wrapped model are not shown here, nor is the org enable/disable invalidation logic referenced. adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:246 — Cached getForLogin resolves cached IDs via getById but does not re-apply getLoginPredicate or the organizationId/mode match to the fresh model. Any missed or late invalidation therefore exposes non-login IDPs directly, and OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean only compensates for isEnabled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the new cached getForLogin() path returns the cached internalIds and resolves them via session.identityProviders().getById(id) without re-applying getLoginPredicate() or re-checking that the resolved model still matches the (mode, organizationId) constraints; it only falls back when idp == null. However, the same caching pattern exists elsewhere (e.g., getByOrganization-style caches), and this PR also adds targeted invalidation logic (registerIDPLoginInvalidation*, including predicate-change and organizationId-change checks) plus an integration test asserting cache invalidation behavior. So the finding describes a real robustness concern (stale cache could surface non-login IDPs if invalidation is missed), but it is not a directly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:381 — Cleanup binds eagerly to the literal alias "alias" (also line 425), so none of the 21 created IDPs is removed and they leak into later tests in the class; the REALM_ONLY count assertions only hold because JUnit's hash order runs this test before testCacheIDPByOrg, which leaks enabled public org-idp-* IDPs the same way.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:401 — Each getForLogin call in the test is the first after population or invalidation, so the cache-hit branch (query.getIDPs(searchKey) != null, the whole point of the change) is never run; no call is repeated to show results come from cache.

adjudication.rationale: In testCacheIDPForLogin, each time session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...) is invoked it is immediately followed by inspecting the cache entry, but the test never repeats the same getForLogin call with an already-populated, non-invalidated cache. That means the code path in InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin where `query != null` and `query.getIDPs(searchKey) != null` (i.e., serving from the cached ID set without reloading from the delegate) is not exercised by this test. The test mainly covers cache creation and invalidation, not cache-hit behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:404 — The Stream returned by getForLogin is discarded and only the cached internal-ID set size is checked, so the test would not catch wrong IDPs, a wrong mix of realm/org IDPs, or differences between the cached path and the delegate path (wrapping, enabled state).

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, the test calls `session.identityProviders().getForLogin(...)` only to populate caches and then asserts against `IdentityProviderListQuery.getIDPs(...).size()` (e.g., around the first assertions after calling `getForLogin(FetchMode.REALM_ONLY, null)`). It never consumes the returned `Stream<IdentityProviderModel>` nor asserts on the actual IDP identities/attributes returned, so it would not detect an incorrect set composition (wrong realm/org mix), ordering/duplication issues, or differences in wrapping/filters between the cached path and delegate path—only the cached internal-id set cardinality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:406 — Each mode is queried with only one organizationId, so the shared per-mode cache key, with different searchKeys (null/"" vs orgaId vs orgbId), and the invalidateObject + merge branch (provider lines 233-240) are never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider#getForLogin`, the cache key is per-realm+mode only (`cacheKeyForLogin(realm, mode)`), while different `organizationId` values are stored under different `searchKey`s inside `IdentityProviderListQuery` (computed as `organizationId != null ? organizationId : ""`). The code has a specific branch for when a cache entry exists but the current `searchKey` is not cached yet (`cached = query.getIDPs(searchKey); if (cached == null) { cache.invalidateObject(cacheKey); ... query = new IdentityProviderListQuery(..., searchKey, cached, query); ... }`). The added test `testCacheIDPForLogin` only ever queries one `organizationId` (`orgaId`) for `FetchMode.ORG_ONLY` and `FetchMode.ALL` (and only `""` for `REALM_ONLY`), so it never exercises this multi-searchKey behavior or the `invalidateObject + merge` branch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/organization/forms/login/freemarker/model/OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean.java:80 — The new isEnabled() re-check is the only thing hiding IDPs of a disabled organization from the login page when the cached login list is not invalidated on org disable, yet no test disables an org (or the org feature) after caching and checks the bean or login page output.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cache for `getForLogin(...)` and invalidation on IDP create/update/remove, plus an `idp.isEnabled()` re-check in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean`. Nothing in the diff shows organization disable (or disabling the org feature) affecting the cached login list, nor that the new `isEnabled()` filter is “the only thing” hiding IDPs for a disabled organization. adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/IdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:254 — The new BROKER_PUBLIC clause in getLoginPredicate is not tested where it matters: no test toggles BROKER_PUBLIC on an already org-linked IDP, and step 4 sets it on a realm-level IDP, where the clause does nothing.

The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises org-linked IDPs with `BROKER_PUBLIC=true` (IDPs 10–19), and in step 4 it sets `BROKER_PUBLIC` on `idp-alias-20` before linking it to an org (so the predicate clause is not actually exercised at the moment of the update, only after linking). There is no test that toggles `BROKER_PUBLIC` on an IDP that is already org-linked (especially from true→false or false→true) to validate the new predicate behavior/invalidation in the scenario where the new clause is the deciding factor.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:428 — Only a non-login (disabled) IDP is removed, so remove() invalidating the login caches for a login-eligible IDP (the new registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp) path) is never verified.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `remove(String alias)` path, the provider now always loads `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` and calls `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`, which invalidates login caches only if `getLoginPredicate().test(idp)` is true. In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, step (1) removes `idp-alias-1`, which is disabled (`setEnabled((i % 2) == 0)`), so it does not qualify for login and therefore does not exercise/verify the behavior when removing a login-eligible IDP should invalidate the login caches. adjudication_records.issue_text: model/infinispan/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/cache/infinispan/idp/InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.java:247 — The stale-entry fallback (cached ID whose getById returns null, which registers an invalidation and falls back to the delegate) has no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new caching logic in `getForLogin(...)` with a stale-entry fallback: when iterating cached internal IDs, if `session.identityProviders().getById(id)` returns `null`, it registers an invalidation and falls back to `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)` (see the new loop in `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider`, around the added `if (idp == null) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKey); return idpDelegate... }`). The new test `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises cache population and invalidation on create/update/remove, but it never creates a condition where the cached ID set contains a missing/deleted IDP while the list cache entry remains present, so this specific fallback path is not covered.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:504 — Step 4 runs an IDP update (BROKER_PUBLIC on a realm-level IDP) and an org link back to back and asserts only afterwards, so it cannot show that the update alone leaves the caches intact or which operation caused the invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin()` step 4, the test performs two state-changing operations in sequence on the same IDP: (1) `update()` setting `OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC`, and (2) linking the IDP to the org via `addIdentityProvider()`, then only afterwards asserts that login caches were cleared. From the diff, those are distinct changes that could independently trigger invalidation (the new invalidation logic considers both login-qualification and org-link changes), so this step cannot attribute which operation caused the invalidation nor demonstrate that the config update alone keeps caches intact.

adjudication_records.issue_text: testsuite/integration-arquillian/tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/testsuite/organization/cache/OrganizationCacheTest.java:505 — Only linking an IDP through the organization API is tested; unlinking an IDP from an org, deleting an org that owns public login IDPs, and toggling IDP enabled/linkOnly (only hideOnLogin is exercised) are not checked for login-cache invalidation.

adjudication.rationale: The added `testCacheIDPForLogin` exercises login-cache population and invalidation for: create/remove of non-login IDPs, updates that do/do-not change login-eligibility (`hideOnLogin`), and a scenario where an IDP is made public and linked to an org via `addIdentityProvider(...)`. It does not cover unlinking (`removeIdentityProvider`-style), deleting an organization after linking public login IDPs, or toggling other predicate-relevant flags like `enabled`/`linkOnly` to verify `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider` login-cache invalidation across those state changes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap for the newly added caching/invalidation logic, not a proven functional defect.
